steps: Stand with the feet together or hip-width, weight even across both soles.
Lengthen the spine, roll the shoulders back and down, and breathe steadily.
cons: Looks simple but easy to collapse the posture without attention

steps: From a lunge, turn the back foot in ~45° and square the hips forward.
Bend the front knee over the ankle and reach the arms overhead; switch sides.
benefits: Strengthens legs and opens the chest
cons: Can strain the lower back if the ribs flare

steps: Step the feet wide, turn the front foot out and bend the front knee over the ankle.
Extend the arms parallel to the floor, gaze over the front hand; switch sides.
cons: Front knee can drift inward and stress the joint

steps: Stand with feet together, bend the knees and sit the hips back as if into a chair.
Reach the arms overhead, keeping the chest lifted; hold and breathe.
cons: Demanding on the knees and lower back if overheld

steps: From a wide stance, turn the front foot out and extend the torso over the front leg.
Rest the front hand on the shin or floor and reach the top arm up; switch sides.
benefits: Stretches the side body and hamstrings
cons: Tendency to round the spine reaching for the floor

steps: Shift weight onto one foot and place the other sole on the inner calf or thigh.
Bring the palms together at the chest or overhead; fix the gaze, then switch sides.
benefits: Strengthens the standing leg and ankles
cons: Avoid pressing the foot into the side of the knee

steps: From Triangle, bend the front knee and step the back foot in, hand to the floor ahead.
Lift the back leg parallel to the floor and open the chest, top arm reaching up; switch sides.
cons: Challenging for the standing ankle and balance

steps: Sit cross-legged with the hips slightly elevated on a folded blanket if needed.
Lengthen the spine, rest the hands on the knees and breathe evenly.
cons: Knees can strain if the hips are tight and unsupported

steps: Sit with the legs extended straight, feet flexed, hands beside the hips.
Lengthen the spine tall and engage the thighs; hold and breathe.
cons: Tight hamstrings cause the lower back to round

steps: Sit and bring the soles of the feet together, letting the knees fall open.
Hold the feet and lengthen the spine; optionally fold forward.
benefits: Opens the hips and inner thighs
cons: Forcing the knees down can strain them

steps: Stack the bent knees, then clasp the hands behind the back (top elbow up, bottom elbow down).
Lengthen the spine and breathe; switch sides.
benefits: Opens the shoulders, chest and hips
cons: Shoulder bind is intense; use a strap

steps: From a cross-legged seat, place each foot on the opposite thigh (only if the knees allow).
Rest the hands on the knees, lengthen the spine and settle the breath.
cons: High risk to the knees if the hips are tight — never force it

steps: Sit with the legs extended straight in front of you.
Hinge from the hips and fold forward, reaching toward the feet with a long spine.
cons: Rounding from the waist can strain the lower back

steps: Stand tall, then hinge from the hips and fold forward, knees soft.
Let the head and neck relax; hold, then roll up slowly to stand.
cons: Coming up too fast can cause light-headedness

steps: Sit with one leg extended and the other foot to the inner thigh.
Fold over the straight leg with a long spine; switch sides.
cons: Avoid forcing the head to the knee — hinge from the hip

steps: From hands and knees, tuck the toes and lift the hips up and back into an inverted V.
Press the hands down, lengthen the spine and reach the heels toward the floor.
cons: Wrist-intensive; can strain the shoulders if overarched

steps: Lie face down with hands under the shoulders, elbows close to the body.
Press lightly into the hands and lift the chest, keeping the hips grounded.
cons: Easy to overarch and compress the lower back

steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet hip-width near the hips.
Press into the feet to lift the hips, rolling the shoulders under; lower slowly.
cons: Avoid turning the head while the neck bears weight

steps: Kneel with hips over knees, hands on the lower back.
Lift the chest and reach the hands toward the heels, leading with the sternum; rise slowly.
benefits: Deeply opens the chest, abdomen and hip flexors
cons: Can strain the lower back and neck; keep the neck long

steps: Lie face down, bend the knees and reach back to hold the ankles.
Kick the feet into the hands to lift the chest and thighs; release slowly.
cons: Intense compression of the lower back

steps: Lie face down, hands by the lower ribs; press into the hands and tops of the feet.
Straighten the arms, lifting the chest and thighs off the floor, shoulders back.
benefits: Opens the chest; key Vinyasa transition
cons: Wrist-intensive; avoid sinking into the shoulders

steps: Lie on your back, tuck the hands under the hips, and lift the chest to rest the crown lightly on the floor.
Keep weight in the forearms, not the head; release slowly.
cons: Compresses the neck if weight rests on the head

steps: Sit with one leg bent, foot outside the opposite thigh.
Lengthen the spine and twist toward the bent knee; switch sides.
cons: Avoid cranking the twist from the neck

steps: Lie on your back, draw one knee in and guide it across the body.
Extend the arms wide and gaze away from the knee; switch sides.
benefits: Gently releases the spine and lower back
cons: Keep both shoulders grounded — don't force the knee down

steps: Kneel and extend one leg out to the side, foot flat.
Reach over the extended leg, side-bending the torso; switch sides.
benefits: Stretches the side body and intercostals
cons: Mind the knee bearing weight on the floor — pad it

steps: On hands and knees, inhale to drop the belly and lift the gaze (cow).
Exhale to round the spine and tuck the chin (cat); flow with the breath.
cons: Keep the wrists comfortable; make a fist if needed

steps: Kneel and sit back on the heels with the spine tall.
Rest the hands on the thighs and breathe evenly.
cons: Pressure on the ankles and knees over long holds

steps: Squat with the feet about hip-width, toes slightly turned out.
Bring the palms together at the chest, elbows pressing the knees open.
benefits: Opens the hips, groin and ankles
cons: Heels may lift if the ankles are tight — support them

steps: Lie back (on a bolster if available) and bring the soles of the feet together, knees open.
Rest the arms by the sides and breathe softly; support the knees with blocks.
benefits: Gently opens the hips and chest
cons: Support the knees to avoid groin strain

steps: Lie on your back and lift the legs and hips, supporting the back with the hands.
Stack the hips over the shoulders with the legs reaching up; lower slowly.
cons: Significant load on the neck — never turn the head in the pose

steps: From Shoulderstand, lower the feet overhead toward the floor.
Support the back with the hands; keep the neck long and lift out slowly.
cons: Heavy load on the neck and upper spine

steps: Interlace the fingers, set the forearms and crown down, and walk the feet in.
Lift the legs with control (against a wall when learning); come down slowly.
cons: Serious neck/cervical risk — learn with supervision

steps: Squat with the hands planted shoulder-width, knees resting on the upper arms.
Lean forward, shifting weight onto the hands and lifting the feet; balance, then lower.
benefits: Builds arm, wrist and core strength
cons: Wrist-intensive; risk of face-plant — pad in front

steps: From plank, shift forward on the toes and lower halfway, elbows hugging the ribs.
Keep the body in one line, shoulders level with the elbows; then transition or rest.
benefits: Builds arm, shoulder and core strength
cons: Shoulders easily dip below elbows, stressing the joint

steps: From plank, roll onto the outer edge of one foot and stack the body, top arm reaching up.
Press the bottom hand down and lift the hips; switch sides.
benefits: Strengthens the wrists, arms, core and obliques
cons: Wrist-intensive; don't let the hips sag

steps: Kneel and sit back on the heels, then fold the torso forward over the thighs.
Rest the forehead down and extend the arms forward or back; breathe softly.
cons: Knee or ankle discomfort — pad them or widen the knees

steps: Sit beside a wall, then swing the legs up it and lie back, hips close to the wall.
Rest the arms by the sides and stay for several minutes; roll to the side to exit.
cons: Come out slowly to avoid light-headedness

steps: Lie flat on your back with the legs relaxed and arms by the sides, palms up.
Close the eyes and release tension from head to toe; rest in stillness.
benefits: Integrates the practice and lowers stress
cons: Lying flat may be uncomfortable late in pregnancy — lie on the side

steps: Sit comfortably with a tall spine.
Use the thumb and ring finger to alternately close each nostril, inhaling and exhaling smoothly.
cons: Stop if you feel dizzy; keep the breath gentle

steps: Sit tall; take a normal inhale, then exhale sharply by snapping the belly in.
Let the inhale happen passively; repeat in short rounds.
cons: Forceful breathing can cause dizziness if overdone

steps: Sit tall, optionally closing the ears with the fingers.
Inhale, then exhale making a steady low humming sound; repeat.
benefits: Soothes the mind and reduces stress
cons: Keep the hum gentle; avoid straining the throat

steps: Sit in a comfortable, stable seat with the spine upright.
Rest the hands on the knees, close the eyes and observe the natural breath.
cons: Discomfort from sitting still — use support as needed
